nodes.name: Homogeneous space $G/H$
nodes.statement: Let G be a locally compact group with left Haar measure $\mu$ and H a closed subgroup of $G$. The left coset space $G/H$ is a homogeneous space with quotient topology. Also, $G$ acts on $G/H$ via $(g,aH) \to gaH$.
nodes.origin_citation: Folland, A course in abstract harmonic analysis

nodes.name: Equality of modular functions on $H$
nodes.statement: We assume that $\Delta_G(h)= \Delta_H(h),$ for all $h\in H,$ where $\Delta_G$ and $\Delta_H$ are the modular function of $G$ and $H$ respectively.

nodes.name: Rho function
nodes.statement: For the pair $(G,H),$ a rho function is a continuous function $\rho: G \to (0,\infty)$ such that $\rho(gh)= \rho(g)$ for all $g\in G$ and $h\in H$

nodes.name: Continuous unitary representation of the homogeneous space $G/H$
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{U}(\mathcal{H}_{\pi})$ be the group consisting of all unitary operators on some Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_{\pi}$. A continuous unitary representation of the homogeneous space $G/H$ is a map $\pi$ from $G/H$ into $\mathcal{U}(\mathcal{H}_{\pi})$ for which $gH \to \langle \pi(gH)\xi, \eta \rangle $ is a continuous map from $G/H \to \mathbb{C}$ such that for each $\xi,\eta \in \mathcal{H}_{\pi}$ and $g,k \in G$, \begin{align*} \pi(gkH) = \pi(gH)\pi(kH)\quad \text{ and } \quad \pi(g^{-1}H) = \pi(gH)^*. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: A unitary-operator-valued map on $G/H$ that is weakly continuous, multiplicative and adjoint-compatible.
nodes.definiendum: continuous unitary representation of the homogeneous space $G/H$

nodes.name: Square integrable representation of $G/H$
nodes.statement: Let $\pi$ be a square integrable representation of $G/H$, i.e. there exists some $\xi \in \mathcal{H}_{\pi}$ and $0< C_{\xi} < \infty$, satisfying \begin{align} C_{\xi} = \int_{G/H} \frac{\rho(e)}{\rho(g)}|\langle \xi, \pi(gH)\xi \rangle|^{2} d\mu_{G/H}(gH). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: A representation of $G/H$ admitting a vector $\xi$ whose matrix coefficient has finite weighted $L^2$ norm $C_\xi$.
differentia: there exists some $\xi \in \mathcal{H}_{\pi}$ and $0< C_{\xi} < \infty$, satisfying \begin{align} C_{\xi} = \int_{G/H} \frac{\rho(e)}{\rho(g)}|\langle \xi, \pi(gH)\xi \rangle|^{2} d\mu_{G/H}(gH). \end{align}

nodes.name: Admissible wavelet
nodes.statement: Then, $\xi$ satisfying (\ref{eq1}) is called an admissible wavelet.

nodes.name: Continuous wavelet transform $W_{\xi}$ on a homogeneous space
nodes.statement: A continuous wavelet transform associated to $\xi$ is a linear operator $W_{\xi} : \mathcal{H}_{\pi} \to C(G/H) $ defined by \begin{align*} (W_{\xi}\eta)(gH) = \left( \frac{\rho(e)}{\rho(g)}\right)^{1/2}\langle \eta, \pi(gH)\xi \rangle \text{ for all } \eta \in \mathcal{H}_{\pi}, gH \in G/H. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: $W_\xi$ maps $\eta$ to the $\rho$-weighted matrix coefficient $\langle \eta,\pi(gH)\xi\rangle$ on $G/H$.

nodes.name: Boundedness of $W_{\xi}$ for irreducible $\pi$
nodes.statement: If $\pi$ is irreducible, then $W_{\xi}$ is a bounded linear operator from Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_{\pi} \text{ into } L^2(G/H)$ and $ L^2(G/H) \simeq L^2(G/H, d\mu_{G/H}),$ where $\mu_{G/H}$ is a relatively $G$-invariant measure on $G/H$ which arises from the rho function $\rho.$
nodes.statement_short: For irreducible $\pi$, $W_\xi$ is bounded from $\mathcal{H}_\pi$ into $L^2(G/H)$ with the $\rho$-induced relatively invariant measure.
conclusions: $W_{\xi}$ is a bounded linear operator from Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_{\pi} \text{ into } L^2(G/H)$
$ L^2(G/H) \simeq L^2(G/H, d\mu_{G/H}),$ where $\mu_{G/H}$ is a relatively $G$-invariant measure on $G/H$ which arises from the rho function $\rho.$

nodes.name: $W_{\xi}(\mathcal{H}_{\pi})$ is a reproducing kernel Hilbert space and ${C_{\xi}}^{-1/2}W_{\xi}$ is an isometry
nodes.statement: Also, $W_{\xi}(\mathcal{H}_{\pi})$ is a reproducing kernel Hilbert space with pointwise bounded kernel and the operator ${C_{\xi}}^{-1/2}W_{\xi}$ is an isometry.
conclusions: $W_{\xi}(\mathcal{H}_{\pi})$ is a reproducing kernel Hilbert space with pointwise bounded kernel
the operator ${C_{\xi}}^{-1/2}W_{\xi}$ is an isometry

nodes.name: Compact $H$ and trivial rho function
nodes.statement: Throughout this section, we assume that $H$ is compact and $\rho(g) = 1$ for all $g \in G$. Thus, $\mu_{G/H} $ is a $G$-invariant measure, i.e. $d\mu_{G/H}(saH) = d\mu_{G/H}(aH)$ for all $s\in G$ and $aH\in G/H$.
nodes.statement_short: Standing hypothesis of Section 2: $H$ compact and $\rho\equiv 1$, so $\mu_{G/H}$ is $G$-invariant.

nodes.name: Continuity of the translation map $a \to {}_af$
nodes.statement: The map $a \to {}_af$ is continuous from $G \to (C_{00}(G/H), \|\cdot\|_{\infty})$ \cite[Proposition 1.25]{kan:13}, where ${}_af(xH) = f(a^{-1}xH)$ for all $a\in G$ and $xH \in G/H$.
assumptions: ${}_af(xH) = f(a^{-1}xH)$ for all $a\in G$ and $xH \in G/H$
conclusions: The map $a \to {}_af$ is continuous from $G \to (C_{00}(G/H), \|\cdot\|_{\infty})$

nodes.name: Continuity of $h(a)=\mu_{G/H}(M\cap aM_0)$
nodes.statement: If $ M_{0}\subseteq M \subseteq G/H$ are such that $ \mu_{G/H}(M) < \infty,$ then the function $h: G \to [0,\infty) $ such that $h(a) = \mu_{G/H}(M\cap aM_{0})$, is continuous.
nodes.statement_short: The overlap measure $a \mapsto \mu_{G/H}(M\cap aM_0)$ is a continuous function on $G$.
conclusions: the function $h: G \to [0,\infty) $ such that $h(a) = \mu_{G/H}(M\cap aM_{0})$, is continuous

nodes.name: Strict measure increment by a translate of $M_0$
nodes.statement: Let $G_0$, the identity component of $G$ be non-compact and $M_{0}\subseteq M \subset G/H$ be such that $ 0 <\mu_{G/H}(M_0)\leq \mu_{G/H}(M) < \infty.$ Then for $\epsilon > 0$ there exists $a \in G_0$ satisfying \begin{align*} \mu_{G/H}(M) < \mu_{G/H}(M\cup aM_{0}) < \mu_{G/H}(M)+\epsilon. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: One can translate $M_0$ by some $a\in G_0$ so that $M\cup aM_0$ has strictly larger but arbitrarily little extra measure.
assumptions: $G_0$, the identity component of $G$ be non-compact
conclusions: there exists $a \in G_0$ satisfying \begin{align*} \mu_{G/H}(M) < \mu_{G/H}(M\cup aM_{0}) < \mu_{G/H}(M)+\epsilon. \end{align*}

nodes.name: Finite dimensionality of finite-support subspaces of $W_{\xi}(\mathcal{H}_{\pi})$
nodes.statement: Since $W_{\xi}(\mathcal{H}_{\pi})$ is a reproducing kernel Hilbert space with point-wise bounded kernel, therefore each subspace of $W_{\xi}(\mathcal{H}_{\pi}) $ consisting of functions having support on a set of finite measure must be of finite dimension \cite{Wilc:00}.
nodes.statement_short: In an RKHS with pointwise bounded kernel, subspaces of functions supported on finite-measure sets are finite dimensional.
assumptions: $W_{\xi}(\mathcal{H}_{\pi})$ is a reproducing kernel Hilbert space with point-wise bounded kernel
conclusions: each subspace of $W_{\xi}(\mathcal{H}_{\pi}) $ consisting of functions having support on a set of finite measure must be of finite dimension

nodes.name: Support of the wavelet transform has infinite measure
nodes.statement: Let $G$ and $H$ be as in Lemma \ref{conn} and $\xi $ be an admissible wavelet associated with an irreducible square integrable representation $\pi$. Then for any $\eta \in \mathcal{H}_{\pi} \setminus \{0\}$, the set $\{gH\in G/H: W_{\xi}\eta(gH)\neq 0 \}$ has infinite measure.
nodes.statement_short: A nonzero wavelet transform on $G/H$ can never be supported on a set of finite measure.
assumptions: $\xi $ be an admissible wavelet associated with an irreducible square integrable representation $\pi$
conclusions: the set $\{gH\in G/H: W_{\xi}\eta(gH)\neq 0 \}$ has infinite measure

nodes.name: Admissible pair $(\xi_1,\xi_2)$
nodes.statement: a pair $ (\xi_1, \xi_2) $ consisting of admissible wavelets in $\mathcal{H}_{\pi}$ is said to be an admissible pair if $\langle \xi_1, \xi_2 \rangle \neq 0$ and $$C_{\xi_1 \xi_2} = \frac{1}{\langle \xi_1,\xi_2 \rangle}\int_{G/H}W_{\xi_1}(\xi_1)(gH)\ \overline{W_{\xi_2}(\xi_2)(gH)}\ d\mu_{G/H}(gH) $$ is a non-zero scalar.
nodes.statement_short: Two admissible wavelets with $\langle\xi_1,\xi_2\rangle\neq 0$ and nonzero cross-admissibility constant $C_{\xi_1\xi_2}$.
nodes.genus: a pair $ (\xi_1, \xi_2) $ consisting of admissible wavelets in $\mathcal{H}_{\pi}$

nodes.name: $W_{\xi_2}^*W_{\xi_1}$ intertwines with $\pi$
nodes.statement: As proved in \cite[Theorem 2.1]{kam:12}, for admissible wavelets $\xi_1,\xi_2$, the operator $ W_{\xi_2}^*W_{\xi_1}$ intertwines with $\pi$. Thus, there exists a scalar $c$ such that $W_{\xi_2}^* W_{\xi_1} = cI$, where $I$ is the identity operator.
nodes.statement_short: The composition $W_{\xi_2}^*W_{\xi_1}$ is an intertwiner, hence a scalar multiple of the identity.
conclusions: the operator $ W_{\xi_2}^*W_{\xi_1}$ intertwines with $\pi$
there exists a scalar $c$ such that $W_{\xi_2}^* W_{\xi_1} = cI$, where $I$ is the identity operator

nodes.name: Weak-sense reconstruction formula for an admissible pair
nodes.statement: If $(\xi_1,\xi_2)$ is an admissible pair, then $\langle \eta_1,\eta_2 \rangle= C_{\xi_1\xi_2}^{-1}\langle W_{\xi_1}\eta_1, W_{\xi_2}\eta_2 \rangle$ which further implies that every $\eta\in \mathcal{H}_{\pi}$ can be decomposed as \begin{align*} \eta &= C_{\xi_1\xi_2}^{-1}\int_{G/H}\left(\frac{\rho(e)}{\rho(g)}\right)^{1/2}W_{\xi_1}\eta(gH)\ \pi(gH)\xi_2\ d\mu(gH), \end{align*} where the integral is defined in the weak sense.
nodes.statement_short: An admissible pair gives a Parseval-type identity and a weak-sense reconstruction of any $\eta$ from $W_{\xi_1}\eta$.
conclusions: $\langle \eta_1,\eta_2 \rangle= C_{\xi_1\xi_2}^{-1}\langle W_{\xi_1}\eta_1, W_{\xi_2}\eta_2 \rangle$

every $\eta\in \mathcal{H}_{\pi}$ can be decomposed as \begin{align*} \eta &= C_{\xi_1\xi_2}^{-1}\int_{G/H}\left(\frac{\rho(e)}{\rho(g)}\right)^{1/2}W_{\xi_1}\eta(gH)\ \pi(gH)\xi_2\ d\mu(gH), \end{align*} where the integral is defined in the weak sense.

nodes.name: Homogeneous approximation property
nodes.statement: An admissible pair $(\xi_1,\xi_2)$ is said to have homogeneous approximation property in $\mathcal{H}_{\pi}$, if for any $\eta \in \mathcal{H}_{\pi}$ and $\epsilon > 0,$ there exists some compact subset $K$ of $G/H$ such that every compact subset $K^{'}$ of $G/H$ with $K \subseteq K^{'}$ satisfies $$\left\|\pi(sH)\eta - C_{\xi_1\xi_2}^{-1}\int_{s\cdot K^{'}}\left(\frac{\rho(e)}{\rho(a)}\right)^{1/2}W_{\xi_1}\pi(sH)\eta(aH)\ \pi(aH)\xi_2\ d\mu_{G/H}(aH)\right\|\leq \epsilon,$$ for all $s \in G.$
nodes.statement_short: Reconstruction of $\pi(sH)\eta$ from the translated compact window $s\cdot K'$ is uniformly $\epsilon$-accurate in $s$.
differentia: for any $\eta \in \mathcal{H}_{\pi}$ and $\epsilon > 0,$ there exists some compact subset $K$ of $G/H$ such that every compact subset $K^{'}$ of $G/H$ with $K \subseteq K^{'}$ satisfies $$\left\|\pi(sH)\eta - C_{\xi_1\xi_2}^{-1}\int_{s\cdot K^{'}}\left(\frac{\rho(e)}{\rho(a)}\right)^{1/2}W_{\xi_1}\pi(sH)\eta(aH)\ \pi(aH)\xi_2\ d\mu_{G/H}(aH)\right\|\leq \epsilon,$$ for all $s \in G.$

nodes.name: Every admissible pair possesses the homogeneous approximation property
nodes.statement: Let $G/H$ be a $\sigma $-compact homogeneous space with an irreducible square integrable representation $\pi$. Then every admissible pair $(\xi_1,\xi_2)$ possesses homogeneous approximation property in $\mathcal{H}_{\pi}$.
assumptions: $G/H$ be a $\sigma $-compact homogeneous space with an irreducible square integrable representation $\pi$
conclusions: every admissible pair $(\xi_1,\xi_2)$ possesses homogeneous approximation property in $\mathcal{H}_{\pi}$

nodes.name: Similitude group $G=(\mathbb{R}^+\times S0(n))\ltimes \mathbb{R}^n$
nodes.statement: We now consider similitude group $ G=(\mathbb{R}^+\times S0(n))\ltimes \mathbb{R}^n,$ with group operation $$(a,r_{\theta},t)(a_1,{r_{\theta}}_1,t_1) = (aa_1,r_{\theta}{r_{\theta}}_1, t+ ar_{\theta}t_1 ). $$ The left Haar measure on $G$ is given by $ \frac{dad\theta dt}{a^{n+1}}.$
differentia: The left Haar measure on $G$ is given by $ \frac{dad\theta dt}{a^{n+1}}.$

nodes.name: Square integrable irreducible representation of the similitude group
nodes.statement: The mapping $\pi: G \to \mathcal{U}(L^2(\mathbb{R}^n))$ defined by $$\pi(a,r_{\theta},t)f(x) = a^{-n/2} \psi\left(r_{\theta}^{-1}\left(\frac{x-t}{a}\right)\right)$$ is a square integrable irreducible representation of $G$. For $\psi\in L^2(\mathbb{R}^n)$, $$C_{\psi} = \int_{\mathbb{R}^{+}}\int_{S0(n)}\frac{\widehat{|\psi}(ar_\theta^{-1}(\omega))|^2}{a}\ da\ d\theta,$$ is independent of almost every $\omega \in \mathbb{R}^n$ (see \cite{ali;00}).
nodes.statement_short: The dilation-rotation-translation representation on $L^2(\mathbb{R}^n)$ is square integrable irreducible with $\omega$-independent constant $C_\psi$.
conclusions: The mapping $\pi: G \to \mathcal{U}(L^2(\mathbb{R}^n))$ defined by $$\pi(a,r_{\theta},t)f(x) = a^{-n/2} \psi\left(r_{\theta}^{-1}\left(\frac{x-t}{a}\right)\right)$$ is a square integrable irreducible representation of $G$.
$$C_{\psi} = \int_{\mathbb{R}^{+}}\int_{S0(n)}\frac{\widehat{|\psi}(ar_\theta^{-1}(\omega))|^2}{a}\ da\ d\theta,$$ is independent of almost every $\omega \in \mathbb{R}^n$

nodes.name: $\omega$-independence of the cross-admissibility constant $C_{\psi_1\psi_2}$
nodes.statement: Also, for an admissible pair $(\psi_1,\psi_2)$, $$C_{\psi_1\psi_2} = \int_{\mathbb{R}^{+}}\int_{S0(n)}\frac{\overline{\widehat{\psi_1}(ar_\theta^{-1}(\omega))}\ \widehat{\psi_2}(ar_\theta^{-1}(\omega))}{a}\ da\ d\theta$$ is independent of $\omega$ upto a measure zero set.
conclusions: $$C_{\psi_1\psi_2} = \int_{\mathbb{R}^{+}}\int_{S0(n)}\frac{\overline{\widehat{\psi_1}(ar_\theta^{-1}(\omega))}\ \widehat{\psi_2}(ar_\theta^{-1}(\omega))}{a}\ da\ d\theta$$ is independent of $\omega$ upto a measure zero set.

nodes.name: Fourier transform of the windowed reconstruction $f_{A_1A_2}$
nodes.statement: Let $(\psi_1,\psi_2)$ be an admissible pair in $L^2(\mathbb{R}^n)$. For $f\in L^2(\mathbb{R}^n)$ and $A_2 > A_1 > 0,$ define \begin{align*} f_{A_1A_2}(x)= C_{\psi_1\psi_2}^{-1}\int_{A_1}^{A_2}\int_{S0(n)}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \langle f, \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_1\rangle\ \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_2(x)\ \frac{dtd\theta da}{a^{n+1}}. \end{align*} Then, $f_{A_1A_2} \in L^2(\mathbb{R}^n)$ and \begin{align*} \widehat{{f_{A_1A_2}}}(\omega) = C_{\psi_1\psi_2}^{-1}\widehat{f}(\omega)\int_{A_1}^{A_2}\int_{S0(n)} \widehat{\psi_{1}}(ar_\theta^{-1}(\omega))\ \widehat{\psi_2}(ar_\theta^{-1}(\omega))\ \frac{d\theta da}{a}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: The scale-band reconstruction $f_{A_1A_2}$ lies in $L^2$ and acts on the Fourier side as multiplication by a band-limited factor.
conclusions: $f_{A_1A_2} \in L^2(\mathbb{R}^n)$

\begin{align*} \widehat{{f_{A_1A_2}}}(\omega) = C_{\psi_1\psi_2}^{-1}\widehat{f}(\omega)\int_{A_1}^{A_2}\int_{S0(n)} \widehat{\psi_{1}}(ar_\theta^{-1}(\omega))\ \widehat{\psi_2}(ar_\theta^{-1}(\omega))\ \frac{d\theta da}{a}. \end{align*}

nodes.name: Pointwise homogeneous approximation property on the similitude group
nodes.statement: Let $(\psi_1,\psi_2)$ be an admissible pair in $L^2(\mathbb{R}^n)$ and $f\in L^2(\mathbb{R}^n)$ with $\widehat{f} \in L^1(\mathbb{R}^n)$. Then for any $\epsilon,p > 0$, there exist $A_2 > A_1 > 0 $ such that for any $(a,r_{\theta},t) \in G$ with $0< p\leq a$ and $0 < A_1^{'}\leq A_1$, $A_2^{'} \geq A_2,$ the following holds \begin{align*} &\left\|\pi(a,r_{\theta},t)f(x)-\left(C_{\psi_1\psi_2}^{-1}\int_{A_1^{'}a}^{A_2^{'}a}\int_{S0(n)}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}\langle \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)f,\pi(a_1,{r_{\theta}}_1,t_1)\psi_1\rangle\right.\right.\\ &\qquad\qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \left.\left.\times \pi(a_1,{r_{\theta}}_1,t_1)\psi_2(x)\ \frac{dt_1d\theta_1da_1}{a_1^{n+1}} \right)\right\|_{\infty}\leq \epsilon. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: A single scale band $[A_1'a, A_2'a]$ reconstructs $\pi(a,r_\theta,t)f$ uniformly to within $\epsilon$ in sup-norm, for all scales $a\geq p$.
assumptions: $(a,r_{\theta},t) \in G$ with $0< p\leq a$ and $0 < A_1^{'}\leq A_1$, $A_2^{'} \geq A_2,$
conclusions: there exist $A_2 > A_1 > 0 $ such that for any $(a,r_{\theta},t) \in G$ with $0< p\leq a$ and $0 < A_1^{'}\leq A_1$, $A_2^{'} \geq A_2,$ the following holds \begin{align*} &\left\|\pi(a,r_{\theta},t)f(x)-\left(C_{\psi_1\psi_2}^{-1}\int_{A_1^{'}a}^{A_2^{'}a}\int_{S0(n)}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}\langle \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)f,\pi(a_1,{r_{\theta}}_1,t_1)\psi_1\rangle\right.\right.\\ &\qquad\qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \left.\left.\times \pi(a_1,{r_{\theta}}_1,t_1)\psi_2(x)\ \frac{dt_1d\theta_1da_1}{a_1^{n+1}} \right)\right\|_{\infty}\leq \epsilon. \end{align*}

nodes.name: Type I unimodular factors $A$, $B$ and automorphism map $\tau$
nodes.statement: Let $A$ and $B$ be locally compact, second countable, unimodular, group of type I and $\tau$ be a map from $B$ to $\text{Aut(A)},$ where $\text{Aut}(A)$ is a group of automorphism of $A$.
nodes.section: Wavelet group of the form $B\ltimes A$

nodes.name: Wavelet group $G = B\ltimes_{\tau} A$
nodes.statement: Let $G = B\ltimes_{\tau} A$ with group operation $(b,a)(b_1,a_1) = (bb_1, a\tau_{b}(a_1))$. The left Haar measure $\mu$ on $G$ is given by $d\mu(b,a)= \delta_{\tau}(b)\ da\ db$, where $\delta_{\tau}$ is a positive homomorphism of $B$ satisfying $d(a) = \delta_{\tau}(b)\ d(\tau_{b}(a)).$
nodes.section: Wavelet group of the form $B\ltimes A$
nodes.statement_short: The semidirect product $B\ltimes_\tau A$ with Haar measure weighted by the modulus $\delta_\tau$ of $\tau$.
differentia: The left Haar measure $\mu$ on $G$ is given by $d\mu(b,a)= \delta_{\tau}(b)\ da\ db$, where $\delta_{\tau}$ is a positive homomorphism of $B$ satisfying $d(a) = \delta_{\tau}(b)\ d(\tau_{b}(a)).$

nodes.name: Representation $\pi$ of $G$ on $L^2(A)$
nodes.statement: Define a representation $\pi$ of $G$ on Hilbert space $L^2(A)$ such that $$\pi(b,a)f(x)= f_{ba}(x)= \delta_{\tau}(b)^{1/2}f(\tau_{b^{-1}}(a^{-1}x)).$$
nodes.section: Wavelet group of the form $B\ltimes A$
nodes.genus: a representation $\pi$ of $G$ on Hilbert space $L^2(A)$

nodes.name: Feasible wavelet
nodes.statement: A function $\psi \in L^1\cap L^2(A)$ is said to be a feasible wavelet, if there exists a constant $0< C_{\psi} < \infty$ such that for almost every $\gamma \in \widehat{A}$ and for all $f,g \in L^1\cap L^2(A)$ \begin{flalign*} &\int_{B} \text{tr}(\gamma(f)\gamma(g)\gamma(\psi \circ \tau_{b^{-1}})^\star\gamma(\psi \circ \tau_{b^{-1}} ))\ \delta_{\tau}^2(b)\ d(b) = C_{\psi}\ \text{tr}(\gamma(f)\gamma(g)). \end{flalign*}
nodes.section: Wavelet group of the form $B\ltimes A$
nodes.statement_short: A wavelet whose $B$-integrated trace expression reproduces $\mathrm{tr}(\gamma(f)\gamma(g))$ up to a finite constant $C_\psi$.
differentia: there exists a constant $0< C_{\psi} < \infty$ such that for almost every $\gamma \in \widehat{A}$ and for all $f,g \in L^1\cap L^2(A)$ \begin{flalign*} &\int_{B} \text{tr}(\gamma(f)\gamma(g)\gamma(\psi \circ \tau_{b^{-1}})^\star\gamma(\psi \circ \tau_{b^{-1}} ))\ \delta_{\tau}^2(b)\ d(b) = C_{\psi}\ \text{tr}(\gamma(f)\gamma(g)). \end{flalign*}

nodes.name: Feasibility constant for abelian $A$
nodes.statement: It may be noted that if $A$ is a locally compact abelian group, then for a feasible wavelet $\psi$, $$C_{\psi}= \int_{B}|\widehat{\psi}(\gamma \circ \tau_{b})|^2 db,$$ is independent of almost every $\gamma\in \widehat{A}. $
nodes.section: Wavelet group of the form $B\ltimes A$

nodes.name: Continuous wavelet transform $W_{\psi}$ with respect to a feasible wavelet
nodes.statement: The continuous wavelet transform with respect to a feasible wavelet $\psi$ is an operator $W_{\psi}:L^2(A)\to L^2(G)$ defined as $W_{\psi}f(b,a)= \langle f,\pi(b,a)\psi\rangle.$
nodes.section: Wavelet group of the form $B\ltimes A$
nodes.definiendum: continuous wavelet transform with respect to a feasible wavelet $\psi$

nodes.name: Convolution form of $W_{\psi}f$
nodes.statement: Also, $$W_{\psi}f(b,a)=\int_{A}f(x)\overline{ \delta_{\tau}(b)^{1/2}\psi(\tau_{b^{-1}}(a^{-1}x))}dx = \delta_{\tau}(b)^{1/2}f*(\psi\circ\tau_{b^{-1}})^{\star}(a),$$ where $(\psi\circ\tau_{b^{-1}})^{\star}(x)=\overline{(\psi\circ\tau_{b^{-1}})(x^{-1})}$.
nodes.section: Wavelet group of the form $B\ltimes A$
nodes.statement_short: $W_\psi f(b,a)$ equals a $\delta_\tau$-weighted convolution of $f$ with the involuted dilated wavelet.

nodes.name: Orthogonality relation $\langle W_{\psi}f,W_{\psi}g\rangle = C_{\psi}\langle f,g \rangle$
nodes.statement: Let $\psi$ be a feasible wavelet and $f,g\in L^2(A)$. Then $\langle W_{\psi}f,W_{\psi}g\rangle = C_{\psi}\langle f,g \rangle$.
nodes.section: Wavelet group of the form $B\ltimes A$
conclusions: $\langle W_{\psi}f,W_{\psi}g\rangle = C_{\psi}\langle f,g \rangle$

nodes.name: $W_{\psi}(L^2(A))$ is a reproducing kernel Hilbert space
nodes.statement: In fact, one can show that $W_{\psi}(L^2(A))$ is a reproducing kernel Hilbert space with point-wise bounded kernel $k$ given by $$k((b,a),(b',a'))= \frac{1}{C_{\psi}}\langle \psi_{b'a'}, \psi_{ba}\rangle. $$
nodes.section: Wavelet group of the form $B\ltimes A$
conclusions: $W_{\psi}(L^2(A))$ is a reproducing kernel Hilbert space with point-wise bounded kernel $k$ given by $$k((b,a),(b',a'))= \frac{1}{C_{\psi}}\langle \psi_{b'a'}, \psi_{ba}\rangle. $$

nodes.name: Infinite measure of the support of $W_{\psi}f$ on a wavelet group
nodes.statement: Let $G = B\ltimes_{\tau} A$ be an abstract wavelet group with $A_0$ non compact and $\psi \in L^2(A)$ be a feasible wavelet. If $0\neq f \in L^2(A)$, then the set $\{ (b,a):W_{\psi}f(b,a) \neq 0\} $ has infinite measure.
nodes.section: Wavelet group of the form $B\ltimes A$
nodes.statement_short: The wavelet-group analogue of the infinite-support theorem for feasible wavelets.
assumptions: $G = B\ltimes_{\tau} A$ be an abstract wavelet group with $A_0$ non compact
conclusions: the set $\{ (b,a):W_{\psi}f(b,a) \neq 0\} $ has infinite measure

nodes.name: Lower estimate for the norm of the wavelet transform outside a small set
nodes.statement: Let $G = B\ltimes_{\tau} A$ be an abstract wavelet group and $\psi \in L^2(A)$ be a feasible wavelet. Let $M\subset G$ be such that $\mu(M)\leq \frac{\sqrt{C_{\psi}}}{\|\psi\|}.$ Then for any $f \in L^2(A)$, \begin{align*} \| W_{\psi}f - \chi_{M}W_{\psi}f\|\geq \sqrt{C_{\psi}}\left(1 - \frac{\|\psi\|\ {\mu(M)}^{1/2}}{\sqrt{C_{\psi}}}\right)\|f\|. \end{align*}
nodes.section: Wavelet group of the form $B\ltimes A$
nodes.statement_short: Truncating $W_\psi f$ to a small set $M$ leaves at least a fixed fraction of its norm.
assumptions: $G = B\ltimes_{\tau} A$ be an abstract wavelet group
conclusions: \begin{align*} \| W_{\psi}f - \chi_{M}W_{\psi}f\|\geq \sqrt{C_{\psi}}\left(1 - \frac{\|\psi\|\ {\mu(M)}^{1/2}}{\sqrt{C_{\psi}}}\right)\|f\|. \end{align*}

nodes.name: Heisenberg inequality for the Fourier transform on $L\times \mathbb{R}$
nodes.statement: For almost all $b\in B$, using Heisenberg inequality for Fourier transform on $L\times \mathbb{R}$ (see \cite{bans;15}), we have \begin{align*} &\Big(\int_{L}\int_{\mathbb{R}}|t|^2|W_{\psi}f(b,l,t)|^2dl\ dt\Big)^{1/2}\Big(\int_{\widehat{L}}\int_{\mathbb{R}}|\gamma|^2\|(\delta, \gamma)W_{\psi}f(b,\cdot,\cdot)\|_{\text{HS}}^2\ d\delta\ d\gamma \Big)^{1/2}\\ & \geq \frac{1}{2}\int_{L}\int_{\mathbb{R}}|W_{\psi}f(b,l,t)|^2dl\ dt \end{align*}
nodes.section: Wavelet group of the form $B\ltimes A$
nodes.statement_short: Classical Heisenberg uncertainty inequality on $L\times\mathbb{R}$, applied fibrewise in $b$ to $W_\psi f$.
conclusions: \begin{align*} &\Big(\int_{L}\int_{\mathbb{R}}|t|^2|W_{\psi}f(b,l,t)|^2dl\ dt\Big)^{1/2}\Big(\int_{\widehat{L}}\int_{\mathbb{R}}|\gamma|^2\|(\delta, \gamma)W_{\psi}f(b,\cdot,\cdot)\|_{\text{HS}}^2\ d\delta\ d\gamma \Big)^{1/2}\\ & \geq \frac{1}{2}\int_{L}\int_{\mathbb{R}}|W_{\psi}f(b,l,t)|^2dl\ dt \end{align*}

nodes.name: Heisenberg type inequality for the wavelet transform
nodes.statement: Let $G = B \ltimes_{\tau}(L\times \mathbb{R})$ be a wavelet group, where $L$ is a compact group and $\psi$ be a feasible wavelet. Then for any $f\in L^2(\mathbb{R})$, we have \begin{align*} &\left(\int_{B}\int_{L}\int_{\mathbb{R}}|t|^2|W_{\psi}f(b,l,t)|^2\delta_{\tau}(b) dt\ dl\ db \right)^{1/2} \left( \int_{\widehat{L}}\int_{\widehat{R}}|\gamma|^2\|(\delta,\gamma)f\|^2_{\text{HS}}\ d\delta\ d\gamma\right)^{1/2}\\ &\geq\frac{\sqrt{C_{\psi}}}{2}||f||^2. \end{align*}
nodes.section: Wavelet group of the form $B\ltimes A$
nodes.statement_short: Time-frequency spread of $W_\psi f$ times frequency spread of $f$ is bounded below by $\tfrac{\sqrt{C_\psi}}{2}\|f\|^2$.
assumptions: $G = B \ltimes_{\tau}(L\times \mathbb{R})$ be a wavelet group, where $L$ is a compact group
conclusions: \begin{align*} &\left(\int_{B}\int_{L}\int_{\mathbb{R}}|t|^2|W_{\psi}f(b,l,t)|^2\delta_{\tau}(b) dt\ dl\ db \right)^{1/2} \left( \int_{\widehat{L}}\int_{\widehat{R}}|\gamma|^2\|(\delta,\gamma)f\|^2_{\text{HS}}\ d\delta\ d\gamma\right)^{1/2}\\ &\geq\frac{\sqrt{C_{\psi}}}{2}||f||^2. \end{align*}

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.1
nodes.statement: Let $C_{00}(G/H)$ be the space of continuous functions with compact support. Since $\chi_{M_0} \in L^1(G/H)$ and $C_{00}(G/H)$ is dense in $L^{1}(G/H),$ therefore we choose $f \in C_{00}(G/H)$ such that $\| \chi_{M_0} - f \|_{1} < \epsilon$, where $ \epsilon > 0$ is arbitrary. Then, we consider \begin{flalign*} |h(a)-h(b)| &\leq \int_{G/H} \left|\left(\chi_{aM_0} - {}_af\right)(xH)\right|d\mu_{G/H}(xH)&\\ &\qquad + \int_{M} \left|\left({}_af-{}_bf\right)(xH)\right|d\mu_{G/H}(xH)&\\ &\qquad + \int_{G/H} \left|\left({}_bf -\chi_{bM_0}\right)(xH)\right|d\mu_{G/H}(xH)&\\ &= 2\|\chi_{M_0} - f \|_1 + \int_{M} \left|\left({}_af- {}_bf\right)(xH)\right|d\mu_{G/H}(xH) &\\ & < 2\epsilon + \int_{M} \left|\left({}_af- {}_bf\right)(xH)\right|d\mu_{G/H}(xH). \end{flalign*} \noindent The map $a \to {}_af$ is continuous from $G \to (C_{00}(G/H), \|\cdot\|_{\infty})$ \cite[Proposition 1.25]{kan:13}, where ${}_af(xH) = f(a^{-1}xH)$ for all $a\in G$ and $xH \in G/H$. Hence, $h$ is a continuous function.
nodes.statement_short: Approximate $\chi_{M_0}$ by a compactly supported continuous $f$ in $L^1$ and use continuity of translation.

nodes.name: Choose a compactly supported approximant of $\chi_{M_0}$
nodes.statement: Let $C_{00}(G/H)$ be the space of continuous functions with compact support. Since $\chi_{M_0} \in L^1(G/H)$ and $C_{00}(G/H)$ is dense in $L^{1}(G/H),$ therefore we choose $f \in C_{00}(G/H)$ such that $\| \chi_{M_0} - f \|_{1} < \epsilon$, where $ \epsilon > 0$ is arbitrary.
nodes.statement_short: Pick $f\in C_{00}(G/H)$ with $\|\chi_{M_0}-f\|_1<\epsilon$ by density.

nodes.name: Three-term estimate of $|h(a)-h(b)|$
nodes.statement: Then, we consider \begin{flalign*} |h(a)-h(b)| &\leq \int_{G/H} \left|\left(\chi_{aM_0} - {}_af\right)(xH)\right|d\mu_{G/H}(xH)&\\ &\qquad + \int_{M} \left|\left({}_af-{}_bf\right)(xH)\right|d\mu_{G/H}(xH)&\\ &\qquad + \int_{G/H} \left|\left({}_bf -\chi_{bM_0}\right)(xH)\right|d\mu_{G/H}(xH)&\\ &= 2\|\chi_{M_0} - f \|_1 + \int_{M} \left|\left({}_af- {}_bf\right)(xH)\right|d\mu_{G/H}(xH) &\\ & < 2\epsilon + \int_{M} \left|\left({}_af- {}_bf\right)(xH)\right|d\mu_{G/H}(xH). \end{flalign*}
nodes.statement_short: Split $|h(a)-h(b)|$ by the triangle inequality into two approximation terms plus a translation-difference term.

nodes.name: Invoke continuity of translation and conclude
nodes.statement: \noindent The map $a \to {}_af$ is continuous from $G \to (C_{00}(G/H), \|\cdot\|_{\infty})$ \cite[Proposition 1.25]{kan:13}, where ${}_af(xH) = f(a^{-1}xH)$ for all $a\in G$ and $xH \in G/H$. Hence, $h$ is a continuous function.
nodes.statement_short: Continuity of $a\mapsto {}_af$ makes the remaining term small, so $h$ is continuous.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.2
nodes.statement: Define $h: G_0 \to \mathbb{R}^+$ by $h(a) = \mu_{G/H}(M\cup aM_{0}).$ Since $\mu_{G/H}$ is $G$-invariant, therefore $h(a) = \mu_{G/H}(M)+\mu_{G/H}(M_0) - \mu_{G/H}(M\cap aM_0).$ Then by Lemma \ref{cont}, $h$ is a continuous function. Also $\mu_{G/H}$ is regular, so there exists a compact subset $K$ of $M$ such that $\mu_{G/H}(M\setminus K) < \mu_{G/H}(M_0)/2.$ Let $K = \{xH: x\in E \}$, where $E$ is a compact subset of $G$. Thus, $S = EHE^{-1}$ is a compact subset of $G$. Choose $a \in G_0\setminus S.$ For such a choice of $a,$ we have $ aK \cap K = \phi$. Moreover, \begin{align*} aM_0\cap K &= a(M_0 \cap (K \cup K^{'}))\cap K\\ &= (aM_0 \cap aK \cap K)\cup (a(M_0 \cap K^{'})\cap K)\\ &= a(M_0 \cap K^{'})\cap K \subseteq a(M_0 \cap K^{'}). \end{align*} Therefore, it follows that $$\mu_{G/H}(aM_0 \cap K)\leq \mu_{G/H}(a(M_0\cap K^{'}))= \mu_{G/H}(M_0\setminus K) < \mu_{G/H}(M_0)/2.$$ Again, we have \begin{flalign*} h(a)&= \mu_{G/H}(M\cup aM_0) &\\ &= \mu_{G/H}((M\cap K)\cup (M\cap K^{'})\cup (aM_0\cap K)\cup ( aM_{0}\cap K^{'}))&\\ &\geq \mu_{G/H}( (M\cap K)\cup ( aM_{0}\cap K^{'})) &\\ &= \mu_{G/H}(M)- \mu_{G/H}(M\cap K^{'})+ \mu_{G/H}(aM_0)- \mu_{G/H}(aM_0\cap K)&\\ &> \mu_{G/H}(M) = h(e). \end{flalign*} Thus, $h$ is a non-constant continuous function on the connected set $G_{0}$. So, we can choose $a \in G_{0}$ such that \begin{align*} \mu_{G/H}(M) = h(e) < h(a) = \mu_{G/H}(M\cup aM_{0}) < \mu_{G/H}(M)+\epsilon = h(e)+ \epsilon.\hspace{1cm}\qedhere \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Show $h(a)=\mu(M\cup aM_0)$ is continuous and non-constant on the connected set $G_0$, then use the intermediate value property.

nodes.name: Define $h$ and establish its continuity
nodes.statement: Define $h: G_0 \to \mathbb{R}^+$ by $h(a) = \mu_{G/H}(M\cup aM_{0}).$ Since $\mu_{G/H}$ is $G$-invariant, therefore $h(a) = \mu_{G/H}(M)+\mu_{G/H}(M_0) - \mu_{G/H}(M\cap aM_0).$ Then by Lemma \ref{cont}, $h$ is a continuous function.
nodes.statement_short: Set $h(a)=\mu_{G/H}(M\cup aM_0)$, rewrite via $G$-invariance, and get continuity from Lemma 2.1.

nodes.name: Choose a compact $K$ and a translate disjoint from it
nodes.statement: Also $\mu_{G/H}$ is regular, so there exists a compact subset $K$ of $M$ such that $\mu_{G/H}(M\setminus K) < \mu_{G/H}(M_0)/2.$ Let $K = \{xH: x\in E \}$, where $E$ is a compact subset of $G$. Thus, $S = EHE^{-1}$ is a compact subset of $G$. Choose $a \in G_0\setminus S.$ For such a choice of $a,$ we have $ aK \cap K = \phi$.
nodes.statement_short: Use regularity to find compact $K\subset M$ and pick $a\in G_0\setminus EHE^{-1}$ so that $aK\cap K=\phi$.

nodes.name: Set-theoretic reduction of $aM_0\cap K$
nodes.statement: Moreover, \begin{align*} aM_0\cap K &= a(M_0 \cap (K \cup K^{'}))\cap K\\ &= (aM_0 \cap aK \cap K)\cup (a(M_0 \cap K^{'})\cap K)\\ &= a(M_0 \cap K^{'})\cap K \subseteq a(M_0 \cap K^{'}). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Decompose $aM_0\cap K$ and show it is contained in $a(M_0\cap K')$.

nodes.name: Bound the measure of $aM_0\cap K$
nodes.statement: Therefore, it follows that $$\mu_{G/H}(aM_0 \cap K)\leq \mu_{G/H}(a(M_0\cap K^{'}))= \mu_{G/H}(M_0\setminus K) < \mu_{G/H}(M_0)/2.$$
nodes.statement_short: Conclude $\mu_{G/H}(aM_0\cap K)<\mu_{G/H}(M_0)/2$.

nodes.name: Show $h(a) > h(e)$
nodes.statement: Again, we have \begin{flalign*} h(a)&= \mu_{G/H}(M\cup aM_0) &\\ &= \mu_{G/H}((M\cap K)\cup (M\cap K^{'})\cup (aM_0\cap K)\cup ( aM_{0}\cap K^{'}))&\\ &\geq \mu_{G/H}( (M\cap K)\cup ( aM_{0}\cap K^{'})) &\\ &= \mu_{G/H}(M)- \mu_{G/H}(M\cap K^{'})+ \mu_{G/H}(aM_0)- \mu_{G/H}(aM_0\cap K)&\\ &> \mu_{G/H}(M) = h(e). \end{flalign*}
nodes.statement_short: Expand $\mu(M\cup aM_0)$ over the four pieces to get the strict inequality $h(a)>h(e)$.

nodes.name: Conclude by connectedness of $G_0$
nodes.statement: Thus, $h$ is a non-constant continuous function on the connected set $G_{0}$. So, we can choose $a \in G_{0}$ such that \begin{align*} \mu_{G/H}(M) = h(e) < h(a) = \mu_{G/H}(M\cup aM_{0}) < \mu_{G/H}(M)+\epsilon = h(e)+ \epsilon.\hspace{1cm}\qedhere \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: A non-constant continuous function on the connected $G_0$ attains an intermediate value giving the required $a$.

nodes.name: Reduce to triviality of the finite-support subspace
nodes.statement: It is enough to show that for every subset $M$ of $ G/H$ with $\mu_{G/H}(M)< \infty $, the set $ \{ F \in W_{\xi}(\mathcal{H}_{\pi}): F = \chi_{M} F \} = \{0\}$.
nodes.statement_short: It suffices to prove that no nonzero element of $W_\xi(\mathcal{H}_\pi)$ is supported in a finite-measure set $M$.

nodes.name: Assume a nonzero $F_0$ supported in $M$ and set $M_0$
nodes.statement: For this assume that $M \subset G/H$ and $0\neq F_{0} \in W_{\xi}(\mathcal{H}_{\pi})$ with $F_0 = \chi_{M}F_0.$ Let $M_0 = \{xH \in G/H : F_{0}(xH)\neq 0 \}$. Then, $$0 < \mu_{G/H}(M_0) \leq \mu_{G/H}(M) < \infty.$$
nodes.statement_short: Suppose $0\neq F_0=\chi_M F_0$ and let $M_0$ be its support, with $0<\mu(M_0)\le\mu(M)<\infty$.

nodes.name: Iterate Lemma 2.2 to build the increasing sequence $\{M_k\}$
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{conn}, there exists $a^{(1)} \in G_0 $ satisfying \[ \mu_{G/H}(M) < \mu_{G/H}(M \cup a^{(1)}M_0) < \mu_{G/H}(M) + \frac{\epsilon}{2}. \] Take $M_1=M$ and $M_2 = M_1 \cup a^{(1)}M_0$ and again using Lemma \ref{conn}, there exists $a^{(2)} \in G_0 $ satisfying \begin{align*} \mu_{G/H}(M_2) < \mu_{G/H}(M_2 \cup a^{(2)}a^{(1)}M_0) < \mu_{G/H}(M_2) + \frac{\epsilon}{2^2}. \end{align*} Continuing in the same manner, we get an increasing sequence $\{M_k\}_{k=1}^{\infty}$ of subsets of $G/H$ given by $$M_k = M_{k-1}\cup a^{(k-1)}\cdots a^{2}a^{1}M_0,$$ where $a^{(i)} \in G_0$ for all $i = 1,2,\dots,k-1$ and satisfy \begin{align} \mu_{G/H}(M_k)< \mu_{G/H}(M_k\cup a^{(k)}a^{(k-1)}\cdots a^{(1)}M_0)< \mu_{G/H}(M_k)+\frac{\epsilon}{2^k}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Repeated use of Lemma 2.2 produces translates $a^{(k)}$ and sets $M_k$ with geometrically small measure increments.

nodes.name: The union $S=\bigcup M_k$ has finite measure
nodes.statement: Define $S = \bigcup\limits_{k=1}^{\infty} M_k.$ Then, \begin{align*} \mu_{G/H}(S) &= \lim\limits_{k \to \infty}\mu_{G/H}(M_k) \leq \lim\limits_{k \to \infty } \left(\mu_{G/H}(M_{k-1})+ \frac{\epsilon}{2^{(k-1)}}\right)\\ &\leq \mu_{G/H}(M)+ \lim\limits_{k \to \infty } \sum\limits_{i=1}^{k-1}\frac{\epsilon}{2^i} =\mu_{G/H}(M)+ \epsilon < \infty. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Summing the geometric increments gives $\mu_{G/H}(S)\le\mu_{G/H}(M)+\epsilon<\infty$.

nodes.name: Define the family $\{F_k\}$ of translated functions
nodes.statement: Consider the family $\{F_{k}\}_{k\in \mathbb{N}}$ of functions on $G/H$ as follows \begin{flalign*} &&&F_{1}(aH)= F_0(aH) &\\ &&&F_{k}(aH) = F_{k-1}((a^{k-1})^{-1}aH) \quad \text{for all } k \geq 2,\text{ and } aH \in G/H. \end{flalign*}
nodes.statement_short: Build $F_k$ by successively translating $F_0$ by the chosen group elements.

nodes.name: Induction: $F_k \in W_{\xi}(\mathcal{H}_{\pi})$ and linear independence
nodes.statement: We will show by induction that $F_{k}\in W_{\xi}(\mathcal{H}_{\pi})$ for all $k \in \mathbb{N}.$ Clearly, $F_1 = F_0 \in W_{\xi}(\mathcal{H}_{\pi}).$ Let us assume that $F_{k-1} \in W_{\xi}(\mathcal{H}_{\pi}),\ \text{i.e.}\ F_{k-1} = W_{\xi}(\eta)$ for some $\eta \in \mathcal{H}_{\pi}.$ Then, \begin{align*} F_{k}(aH) &= W_{\xi}(\eta)((a^{(k-1)})^{-1}aH)\\ &=\left\langle \eta , \pi((a^{(k-1)})^{-1}aH)\xi \right\rangle\\ &= \left\langle \pi(a^{(k-1)}H)\eta, \pi(aH)\xi \right\rangle\\ &= W_{\xi}(\pi({a^{(k-1)}H)}\eta) \end{align*} which implies that $F_{k} \in W_{\xi}(\mathcal{H}_{\pi}).$ Using (\ref{lin-ind}), we conclude that the family $\{F_{k}\}_{k\in \mathbb{N}}$ of functions on $G/H$ is linearly independent vanishing outside the set $S$ of finite measure.
nodes.statement_short: Induction on $k$, using the covariance $W_\xi(\pi(aH)\eta)$, shows each $F_k$ lies in the range and the family is linearly independent.

nodes.name: Contradiction with finite dimensionality and conclusion
nodes.statement: Since $W_{\xi}(\mathcal{H}_{\pi})$ is a reproducing kernel Hilbert space with point-wise bounded kernel, therefore each subspace of $W_{\xi}(\mathcal{H}_{\pi}) $ consisting of functions having support on a set of finite measure must be of finite dimension \cite{Wilc:00}. If $W_{\xi}\eta \in W_{\xi}(\mathcal{H}_{\pi})$ such that $\mu_{G/H}\{xH : W_{\xi}\eta(xH)\neq 0 \}< \infty, $ then $W_{\xi}\eta = 0$ a.e. and hence $\eta = 0.$ Thus, the support of $W_{\xi}\eta$ is a set of infinite measure for every non-zero $\eta \in \mathcal{H}_{\pi}$.
nodes.statement_short: Finite dimensionality of finite-support subspaces of the RKHS forces $\eta=0$, so the support is of infinite measure.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.2

nodes.statement: First we show that $f_{A_1A_2}$ is well defined. For this, we compute \begin{align*} &\int_{A_1}^{A_2}\int_{S0(n)}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \big|\langle f, \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_1\rangle\ \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_2(x)\big|\ \frac{dtd\theta da}{a^{n+1}}\\ &\leq\int_{A_1}^{A_2}\int_{S0(n)}\left( \int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \big|\langle f, \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_1\rangle \big|^2 dt\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\left( \int_{\mathbb{R}^n}\big|\pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_2(x)\big|^2dt \right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\frac{d\theta da}{a^{n+1}}\\ &\leq\int_{A_1}^{A_2}\int_{S0(n)}\left( \int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \big|\langle f, \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_1\rangle \big|^2 dt\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\|\psi_2\|_{2}\ \frac{d\theta da}{a^{n+1}}\\ &\leq \|\psi_2\|_{2}\left(\int_{A_1}^{A_2}\int_{S0(n)}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \big|\langle f, \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_1\rangle \big|^2 \frac{ dtd\theta da}{a^{n+1}}\right)^{1/2}\left(\int_{A_1}^{A_2}\int_{S0(n)}\frac{d\theta da}{a^{n+1}} \right)^{1/2}\\ &=\|\psi_2\|_{2}\sqrt{C_{\psi_1}}\|f\|_2\ n^{-\frac{1}{2}}(A_1^{-n}-A_2^{-n})< \infty. \end{align*} Let $g\in L^1\cap L^2(\mathbb{R}^n)$ be arbitrary. Again, we have \begin{align*} & \int_{\mathbb{R}^n} f_{A_1A_2}(x)\overline{g(x)}\ dx \\ &= C_{\psi_1\psi_2}^{-1} \int_{\mathbb{R}^n}\overline{g(x)}\left(\int_{A_1}^{A_2}\int_{S0(n)}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \langle f, \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_1\rangle \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_2(x)\ \frac{dtd\theta da}{a^{n+1}}\right)dx\\ &=C_{\psi_1\psi_2}^{-1}\int_{A_1}^{A_2}\int_{S0(n)}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \langle f, \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_1\rangle\left(\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}\overline{g(x)}\pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_2(x)dx\right)\ \frac{dtd\theta da}{a^{n+1}}\\ by Riesz representation theorem $f_{A_1A_2}\in L^2(\mathbb{R}^n).$ Now on using Plancherel Theorem, we have \begin{align*} &&&\langle f_{A_1A_2}, g\rangle &\\ &&&= C_{\psi_1\psi_2}^{-1}\int_{A_1}^{A_2}\int_{S0(n)}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \langle f, \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_1\rangle\ \langle \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_2, g\rangle\ \frac{dtd\theta da}{a^{n+1}} & \\ &&&= C_{\psi_1\psi_2}^{-1}\int_{A_1}^{A_2}\int_{S0(n)}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} (f*\pi(a,r_\theta,0)\psi_1^{\star}(t))\ (g*\pi(a,r_\theta,0)\psi_2^{\star}(t))\ \frac{dtd\theta da}{a^{n+1}} &\\ &&&= \widehat{\psi_{1}}(ar_\theta^{-1}(\omega))\ \widehat{\psi_2}(ar_\theta^{-1}(\omega))\frac{dad\theta}{a}.\qquad\qquad \qquad \qquad\qedhere \end{align*}

For this, we compute \begin{align*} &\int_{A_1}^{A_2}\int_{S0(n)}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \big|\langle f, \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_1\rangle\ \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_2(x)\big|\ \frac{dtd\theta da}{a^{n+1}}\\ &\leq\int_{A_1}^{A_2}\int_{S0(n)}\left( \int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \big|\langle f, \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_1\rangle \big|^2 dt\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\left( \int_{\mathbb{R}^n}\big|\pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_2(x)\big|^2dt \right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\frac{d\theta da}{a^{n+1}}\\ &\leq\int_{A_1}^{A_2}\int_{S0(n)}\left( \int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \big|\langle f, \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_1\rangle \big|^2 dt\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\|\psi_2\|_{2}\ \frac{d\theta da}{a^{n+1}}\\ &\leq \|\psi_2\|_{2}\left(\int_{A_1}^{A_2}\int_{S0(n)}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \big|\langle f, \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_1\rangle \big|^2 \frac{ dtd\theta da}{a^{n+1}}\right)^{1/2}\left(\int_{A_1}^{A_2}\int_{S0(n)}\frac{d\theta da}{a^{n+1}} \right)^{1/2}\\ &=\|\psi_2\|_{2}\sqrt{C_{\psi_1}}\|f\|_2\ n^{-\frac{1}{2}}(A_1^{-n}-A_2^{-n})< \infty. \end{align*}

nodes.name: Integrability against a test function via Tonelli
nodes.statement: Let $g\in L^1\cap L^2(\mathbb{R}^n)$ be arbitrary. Then \begin{align*} &\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \left|g(x)f_{A_1A_2}(x)\right|dx \\ &\leq \int_{\mathbb{R}^n}\left(|g(x)| \int_{A_1}^{A_2}\int_{S0(n)}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} |\langle f, \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_1\rangle \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_2(x)|\frac{dtd\theta da}{a^{n+1}} \right)dx\\ & < \infty. \end{align*} Thus, using Tonneli theorem, the function $g(\cdot)\langle f, \pi(\cdot,\cdot,\cdot)\psi_1\rangle \pi(\cdot,\cdot,\cdot)\psi_2(\cdot) $ is integrable.
nodes.statement_short: For $g\in L^1\cap L^2$ the joint integrand is integrable, so Tonelli applies.

nodes.name: Compute the pairing $\int f_{A_1A_2}\overline{g}$
nodes.statement: Again, we have \begin{align*} & \int_{\mathbb{R}^n} f_{A_1A_2}(x)\overline{g(x)}\ dx \\ &= C_{\psi_1\psi_2}^{-1} \int_{\mathbb{R}^n}\overline{g(x)}\left(\int_{A_1}^{A_2}\int_{S0(n)}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \langle f, \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_1\rangle \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_2(x)\ \frac{dtd\theta da}{a^{n+1}}\right)dx\\ &=C_{\psi_1\psi_2}^{-1}\int_{A_1}^{A_2}\int_{S0(n)}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \langle f, \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_1\rangle\left(\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}\overline{g(x)}\pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_2(x)dx\right)\ \frac{dtd\theta da}{a^{n+1}}\\ &=C_{\psi_1\psi_2}^{-1}\int_{A_1}^{A_2}\int_{S0(n)}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \langle f, \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_1\rangle\langle \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_2, g\rangle\ \frac{dtd\theta da}{a^{n+1}}. \end{align*}

nodes.name: Bound the pairing and apply Riesz representation
nodes.statement: Thus, \begin{flalign*} \left|\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} f_{A_1A_2}(x)\overline{g(x)}\ dx\right| & \leq C_{\psi_1\psi_2}^{-1}\int_{\mathbb{R}^+}\int_{S0(n)}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}| \langle f, \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_1\rangle\langle \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_2, g\rangle|\ \frac{dtd\theta da}{a^{n+1}}&\\ &\leq C_{\psi_1\psi_2}^{-1}\|f\|_2C_{\psi_1}C_{\psi_2}\|g\|_2. \end{flalign*} Therefore, by Riesz representation theorem $f_{A_1A_2}\in L^2(\mathbb{R}^n).$

nodes.name: Plancherel computation of $\widehat{f_{A_1A_2}}$

\widehat{\psi_2}(a_1 {r_{\theta}}_1^{-1}(\omega))| \ \frac{da_1d\theta_1}{a_1}d\omega \\ &\qquad+ |C_{\psi_1\psi_2}^{-1}|\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}\left|\widehat{\pi(a,r_{\theta},t)f}(\omega)\right|\int_{S0(n)}\int_{A_2^{'}a}^{\infty} |\widehat{\psi_{1}}(a_1{r_\theta}_1^{-1}(\omega))\ \widehat{\psi_2}(a_1 {r_{\theta}}_1^{-1}(\omega))|\ \frac{da_1d\theta_1}{a_1}d\omega. \\ &\leq {r_{\theta}}_1^{-1}(\omega))|\ \frac{da_1d\theta_1}{a_1}d\omega \\ &\qquad+ |C_{\psi_1\psi_2}^{-1}|\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}|a|^{n/2}|\widehat{f}(ar_{\theta}^{-1}\omega)|\int_{S0(n)}\int_{A_2^{'}a}^{\infty} \widehat{\psi_2}(a_1{r_\theta}_1^{-1}(\omega))|\frac{da_1d\theta_1}{a_1}= 0 \end{align*} By Lebesgue dominated convergence theorem, we get \begin{align*} \lim\limits_{A_1^{'} \to 0} nodes.name: Define the low-scale and high-scale tail pieces
nodes.statement: For arbitrary $0 < A_1^{'}< A_{2}^{'}$ and $(a,r_{\theta},t)\in G$ with $p\leq a$, define \begin{flalign*} &f_{A_1^{'}a}(x)=C_{\psi_1\psi_2}^{-1} \int_{0}^{A_1^{'}a}\int_{S0(n)}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}\langle \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)f,\pi(a_1,{r_{\theta_1}},t_1)\psi_1\rangle &\\ & \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \times \pi(a_1,{r_{\theta}}_1,t_1)\psi_2(x)\ \frac{dt_1d\theta_1da_1}{a_1^{n+1}} \end{flalign*} and \begin{flalign*} &f_{A_2^{'}a}(x)=C_{\psi_1\psi_2}^{-1} \int_{A_2^{'}a}^{\infty}\int_{S0(n)}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}\langle \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)f,\pi(a_1,{r_{\theta_1}},t_1)\psi_1\rangle &\\ & \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \times\pi(a_1,{r_{\theta}}_1,t_1)\psi_2(x)\ \frac{dt_1d\theta_1da_1}{a_1^{n+1}}. \end{flalign*}
nodes.statement_short: Introduce $f_{A_1'a}$ and $f_{A_2'a}$ as the integrals over the discarded scale ranges.

nodes.name: Bound the sup-norm error by rescaled Fourier tail integrals
nodes.statement: Then, \begin{align*} &\left\|\pi(a,r_{\theta},t)f(x)-\left(C_{\psi_1\psi_2}^{-1}\int_{A_1^{'}a}^{A_2^{'}a}\int_{S0(n)}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}\left(\langle \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)f,\pi(a_1,{r_{\theta}}_1,t_1)\psi_1\rangle\right)\right.\right.\\ &\qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \left.\left.\times\ \left(\pi(a_1,{r_{\theta}}_1,t_1)\psi_2(x)\right)\ \frac{dt_1d\theta_1da_1}{a_1^{n+1}}\right) \right\|_{\infty}\\ & = \Big\| f_{A_1^{'}a}(x)+ f_{A_2^{'}a}(x) \|_{\infty} \leq \|\widehat{f_{A_1^{'}a}}\|_{1} + \|\widehat{f_{A_2^{'}a}}\Big\|_{1}\\ &\leq|C_{\psi_1\psi_2}^{-1}| \int_{\mathbb{R}^n}\left|\widehat{\pi(a,r_{\theta},t)f}(\omega)\right|\int_{S0(n)}\int_{0}^{A_1^{'}a} |\widehat{\psi_{1}}(a_1 {r_{\theta}}_1^{-1}(\omega))\ \widehat{\psi_2}(a_1 {r_{\theta}}_1^{-1}(\omega))| \ \frac{da_1d\theta_1}{a_1}d\omega \\ &\qquad+ |C_{\psi_1\psi_2}^{-1}|\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}\left|\widehat{\pi(a,r_{\theta},t)f}(\omega)\right|\int_{S0(n)}\int_{A_2^{'}a}^{\infty} |\widehat{\psi_{1}}(a_1{r_\theta}_1^{-1}(\omega))\ \widehat{\psi_2}(a_1 {r_{\theta}}_1^{-1}(\omega))|\ \frac{da_1d\theta_1}{a_1}d\omega. \\ &\leq |C_{\psi_1\psi_2}^{-1}|\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}|a|^{n/2}|\widehat{f}(ar_{\theta}^{-1}\omega)|\int_{S0(n)}\int_{0}^{A_1^{'}a} |\widehat{\psi_{1}}(a_1 {r_{\theta}}_1^{-1}(\omega))\ \widehat{\psi_2}(a_1 {r_{\theta}}_1^{-1}(\omega))|\ \frac{da_1d\theta_1}{a_1}d\omega \\ &\qquad+ |C_{\psi_1\psi_2}^{-1}|\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}|a|^{n/2}|\widehat{f}(ar_{\theta}^{-1}\omega)|\int_{S0(n)}\int_{A_2^{'}a}^{\infty} |\widehat{\psi_{1}}(a_1{r_\theta}_1^{-1}(\omega))\ \widehat{\psi_2}(a_1 {r_{\theta}}_1^{-1}(\omega))|\ \frac{da_1d\theta_1}{a_1}d\omega\\ &\leq |C_{\psi_1\psi_2}^{-1}|\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}|p|^{-n/2}|\widehat{f}(\omega)|\int_{S0(n)}\int_{0}^{A_1^{'}} |\widehat{\psi_{1}}(a_1 {r_{\theta}}_1^{-1}(\omega))\ \widehat{\psi_2}(a_1 {r_{\theta}}_1^{-1}(\omega))|\ \frac{da_1d\theta_1}{a_1}d\omega \\ &\qquad+ |C_{\psi_1\psi_2}^{-1}|\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}|p|^{-n/2}|\widehat{f}(\omega)|\int_{S0(n)}\int_{A_2^{'}}^{\infty} |\widehat{\psi_{1}}(a_1{r_\theta}_1^{-1}(\omega))\ \widehat{\psi_2}(a_1 {r_{\theta}}_1^{-1}(\omega))|\ \frac{da_1d\theta_1}{a_1}d\omega. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Estimate $\|f_{A_1'a}+f_{A_2'a}\|_\infty$ by $L^1$ norms of the Fourier transforms and rescale using $a \geq p$.

nodes.name: Finiteness of the tail integrals by admissibility
nodes.statement: Since both $\psi_1$ and $\psi_2$ are admissible, therefore we get \begin{align} \int_{S0(n)}\int_{0}^{A_1^{'}} |\widehat{\psi_{1}}(a_1{r_\theta}_1^{-1}(\omega))\ \widehat{\psi_2}(a_1{r_\theta}_1^{-1}(\omega))|\frac{da_1d\theta_1}{a_1}\leq C_{\psi_1}C_{\psi_2}< \infty \end{align} and \begin{align} \int_{S0(n)}\int_{A_2^{'}}^{\infty} |\widehat{\psi_{1}}(a_1{r_\theta}_1^{-1}(\omega))\ \widehat{\psi_2}(a_1{r_\theta}_1^{-1}(\omega))|\frac{da_1d\theta_1}{a_1}\leq C_{\psi_1}C_{\psi_2}< \infty. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Admissibility of $\psi_1,\psi_2$ bounds both scale-tail integrals by $C_{\psi_1}C_{\psi_2}<\infty$.

nodes.name: Vanishing of the tail integrals in the limits
nodes.statement: Also, \begin{align*} \lim\limits_{A_1^{'}\to 0}\int_{S0(n)}\int_{0}^{A_1^{'}}|\widehat{\psi_{1}}(a_1{r_\theta}_1^{-1}(\omega))\ \widehat{\psi_2}(a_1{r_\theta}_1^{-1}(\omega))|\frac{da_1d\theta_1}{a_1} =0 \end{align*} and \begin{align*} &\lim\limits_{A_2^{'}\to \infty}\ \int_{S0(n)}\int_{0}^{A_2^{'}} |\widehat{\psi_{1}}(a_1{r_\theta}_1^{-1}(\omega))\ \widehat{\psi_2}(a_1{r_\theta}_1^{-1}(\omega))|\frac{da_1d\theta_1}{a_1} & \\ &\qquad \qquad =\int_{S0(n)}\int_{0}^{\infty} |\widehat{\psi_{1}}(a_1{r_\theta}_1^{-1}(\omega))\ \widehat{\psi_2}(a_1{r_\theta}_1^{-1}(\omega))|\frac{da_1d\theta_1}{a_1}. \end{align*} Thus, \begin{align*} \lim\limits_{A_2^{'}\to \infty} \int_{S0(n)}\int_{A_2^{'}}^{\infty}|\widehat{\psi_{1}}(a_1{r_\theta}_1^{-1}(\omega))\ \widehat{\psi_2}(a_1{r_\theta}_1^{-1}(\omega))|\frac{da_1d\theta_1}{a_1}= 0 \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: As $A_1'\to 0$ and $A_2'\to\infty$ the corresponding scale-tail integrals tend to zero.

nodes.name: Dominated convergence and choice of $A_1, A_2$
nodes.statement: By Lebesgue dominated convergence theorem, we get \begin{align*} \lim\limits_{A_1^{'} \to 0} \int_{\mathbb{R}^n}|\widehat{f}(\omega)|\int_{S0(n)}\int_{0}^{A_1^{'}} |\widehat{\psi_{1}}(a_1{r_\theta}_1^{-1}(\omega))\ \widehat{\psi_2}(a_1 {r_{\theta}}_1^{-1}(\omega))|\ \frac{da_1d\theta_1}{a_1}d\omega = 0. \end{align*} and \begin{align*} \lim\limits_{A_2^{'} \to \infty} \int_{\mathbb{R}^n}|\widehat{f}(\omega)|\int_{S0(n)}\int_{A_2^{'}}^{\infty} |\widehat{\psi_{1}}(a_1{r_\theta}_1^{-1}(\omega))\ \widehat{\psi_2}(a_1 {r_{\theta}}_1^{-1}(\omega))|\ \frac{da_1d\theta_1}{a_1}d\omega = 0. \end{align*} Therefore, we can choose $0 < A_1\leq A_2$ such that for any $(a,r_{\theta},t)$ with $0< p\leq a$ and $0< A_1^{'}\leq A_1, A_2<A_2^{'}$, the conclusion of the theorem holds.
nodes.statement_short: Dominated convergence transfers the vanishing to the $\omega$-integrals, allowing a uniform choice of $A_1\le A_2$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 4.3
nodes.statement: Let $P_R :L^2(G) \to L^2(G) $ be the orthogonal projection from $L^2(G)$ to the closed subspace $W_{\psi}(L^2(A))$ and $P_M :L^2(G) \to L^2(G)$ be the orthogonal projection from $L^2(G)$ to the closed subspace of functions with support contained in $M.$ Now, \begin{align} \| W_{\psi}f - \chi_{M}\cdot W_{\psi}f\| &= \| W_{\psi}f- P_MP_R(W_{\psi}f)\| \nonumber \\ \nonumber & \geq \|W_{\psi}f\| - \|P_MP_R\|\ \|W_{\psi}f\|\\ &= (1-\|P_MP_R\|)\ \sqrt{C_{\psi}}\ \|f\|. \end{align} Now $P_R$ being a projection on a reproducing kernel Hilbert space can be represented by \begin{align*} P_RF(b,a) = \langle F(b^{'},a^{'}), k((b^{'},a^{'}), (b,a)) \rangle, \end{align*} where $F \in L^2(G)$ and $k(.,.)$ is the reproducing kernel. Thus, for every $F\in L^2(G),$ we have \begin{align*} P_MP_RF(b,a) = \int_{G} \chi_{M}(b,a)k((b^{'},a^{'}), (b,a))F(b^{'},a^{'})d\mu(b^{'},a^{'}). \end{align*} From \cite{hal;78}, the operator norm $\|P_MP_R\|$ is given by \begin{flalign*} \| P_MP_R\|^{2} &= \int_{G}\int_{G}|\chi_{M}(b,a)\ k((b^{'},a^{'}),(b,a))|^2\ d\mu(b,a)\ d\mu(b^{'},a^{'})&\\ &=\int_{G}\int_{G}|\chi_{M}(b,a)\frac{1}{C_{\psi}}\langle \psi_{ba}, \psi_{b^{'}a^{'}}\rangle |^2\ d\mu(b,a)\ d\mu(b^{'},a^{'})&\\ &=\frac{1}{C_{\psi}^2}\int_{M} \int_{G}|W_{\psi}\psi_{ba}(b^{'},a^{'})|^2\ d\mu(b^{'},a^{'})\ d\mu(b,a)&\\ &=\frac{1}{C_{\psi}}\int_{M}\|\psi_{ba}\|^2\ d\mu(b,a)&\\ &= \frac{1}{C_{\psi}}\|\psi\|^{2}\ \mu(M). \end{flalign*} On substituting the value $\|P_MP_R\|$ into (\ref{conc}), we get the desired inequality.
nodes.section: Wavelet group of the form $B\ltimes A$
nodes.statement_short: Write the truncation as the composition of two orthogonal projections and compute $\|P_MP_R\|^2 = \|\psi\|^2\mu(M)/C_\psi$ via the reproducing kernel.

nodes.name: Introduce the projections $P_R$ and $P_M$
nodes.statement: Let $P_R :L^2(G) \to L^2(G) $ be the orthogonal projection from $L^2(G)$ to the closed subspace $W_{\psi}(L^2(A))$ and $P_M :L^2(G) \to L^2(G)$ be the orthogonal projection from $L^2(G)$ to the closed subspace of functions with support contained in $M.$

nodes.statement_short: Define the orthogonal projections onto $W_\psi(L^2(A))$ and onto functions supported in $M$.

nodes.name: Lower bound of the truncation error by $1-\|P_MP_R\|$
nodes.statement: Now, \begin{align} \| W_{\psi}f - \chi_{M}\cdot W_{\psi}f\| &= \| W_{\psi}f- P_MP_R(W_{\psi}f)\| \nonumber \\ \nonumber & \geq \|W_{\psi}f\| - \|P_MP_R\|\ \|W_{\psi}f\|\\ &= (1-\|P_MP_R\|)\ \sqrt{C_{\psi}}\ \|f\|. \end{align}

nodes.statement_short: Reverse triangle inequality plus the isometry relation give $\|W_\psi f-\chi_M W_\psi f\|\geq (1-\|P_MP_R\|)\sqrt{C_\psi}\|f\|$.

nodes.name: Kernel representation of $P_R$ and $P_MP_R$
nodes.statement: Now $P_R$ being a projection on a reproducing kernel Hilbert space can be represented by \begin{align*} P_RF(b,a) = \langle F(b^{'},a^{'}), k((b^{'},a^{'}), (b,a)) \rangle, \end{align*} where $F \in L^2(G)$ and $k(.,.)$ is the reproducing kernel. Thus, for every $F\in L^2(G),$ we have \begin{align*} P_MP_RF(b,a) = \int_{G} \chi_{M}(b,a)k((b^{'},a^{'}), (b,a))F(b^{'},a^{'})d\mu(b^{'},a^{'}). \end{align*}
nodes.section: Wavelet group of the form $B\ltimes A$
nodes.statement_short: Express $P_R$ through the reproducing kernel and $P_MP_R$ as an integral operator.

nodes.name: Compute the operator norm $\|P_MP_R\|^2$
nodes.statement: From \cite{hal;78}, the operator norm $\|P_MP_R\|$ is given by \begin{flalign*} \| P_MP_R\|^{2} &= \int_{G}\int_{G}|\chi_{M}(b,a)\ k((b^{'},a^{'}),(b,a))|^2\ d\mu(b,a)\ d\mu(b^{'},a^{'})&\\ &=\int_{G}\int_{G}|\chi_{M}(b,a)\frac{1}{C_{\psi}}\langle \psi_{ba}, \psi_{b^{'}a^{'}}\rangle |^2\ d\mu(b,a)\ d\mu(b^{'},a^{'})&\\ &=\frac{1}{C_{\psi}^2}\int_{M} \int_{G}|W_{\psi}\psi_{ba}(b^{'},a^{'})|^2\ d\mu(b^{'},a^{'})\ d\mu(b,a)&\\ &=\frac{1}{C_{\psi}}\int_{M}\|\psi_{ba}\|^2\ d\mu(b,a)&\\ &= \frac{1}{C_{\psi}}\|\psi\|^{2}\ \mu(M). \end{flalign*}
nodes.section: Wavelet group of the form $B\ltimes A$
nodes.statement_short: The Hilbert-Schmidt computation yields $\|P_MP_R\|^2=\|\psi\|^2\mu(M)/C_\psi$.

nodes.name: Substitute the norm and conclude
nodes.statement: On substituting the value $\|P_MP_R\|$ into (\ref{conc}), we get the desired inequality.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 4.5
nodes.section: Wavelet group of the form $B\ltimes A$
nodes.statement_short: Apply the Heisenberg inequality fibrewise in $b$, integrate in $\delta_\tau(b)db$, use Cauchy-Schwarz with the orthogonality relation, then simplify the frequency factor by feasibility.

nodes.name: Apply the Heisenberg inequality for almost every $b$
nodes.statement: For almost all $b\in B$, using Heisenberg inequality for Fourier transform on $L\times \mathbb{R}$ (see \cite{bans;15}), we have \begin{align*} &\Big(\int_{L}\int_{\mathbb{R}}|t|^2|W_{\psi}f(b,l,t)|^2dl\ dt\Big)^{1/2}\Big(\int_{\widehat{L}}\int_{\mathbb{R}}|\gamma|^2\|(\delta, \gamma)W_{\psi}f(b,\cdot,\cdot)\|_{\text{HS}}^2\ d\delta\ d\gamma \Big)^{1/2}\\ & \geq \frac{1}{2}\int_{L}\int_{\mathbb{R}}|W_{\psi}f(b,l,t)|^2dl\ dt \end{align*}

nodes.statement_short: Use the known Heisenberg inequality on $L\times\mathbb{R}$ to the fibre $W_\psi f(b,\cdot,\cdot)$.

nodes.name: Integrate over $B$ with respect to $\delta_{\tau}(b)db$
nodes.statement: On integrating both sides with respect to the measure $\delta_{\tau}(b)db$, we get \begin{align*} &\int_B\Big(\int_{L}\int_{\mathbb{R}}|t|^2|W_{\psi}f(b,l,t)|^2 dl\ dt\Big)^{1/2}\Big(\int_{\widehat{L}}\int_{\mathbb{R}}|\gamma|^2\|(\delta, \gamma)W_{\psi}f(b,\cdot,\cdot)\|_{\text{HS}}^2 \ d\delta\ d\gamma \Big)^{1/2} \delta_{\tau}(b)db \\ &\geq \frac{1}{2}\int_{B}\int_{L}\int_{\mathbb{R}}|W_{\psi}f(b,l,t)|^2 \delta_{\tau}(b) dl\ dt\ db. \end{align*}

nodes.statement_short: Integrate the fibrewise inequality against the weight $\delta_\tau(b)$.

nodes.name: Cauchy-Schwarz and the orthogonality relation
nodes.statement: Using Lemma \ref{isom} and Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, it follows that \begin{flalign} &\left(\int_B\int_{L}\int_{\mathbb{R}}|t|^2|W_{\psi}f(b,l,t)|^2 \delta_{\tau}(b) dl\ dt\ db\right)^{1/2}\nonumber &\\ & \times \left(\int_B\int_{\widehat{L}}\int_{\mathbb{R}}|\gamma|^2\|(\delta, \gamma)W_{\psi}f(b,\cdot,\cdot)\|_{\text{HS}}^2\ \delta_{\tau}(b) d\delta\ d\gamma\ db \right)^{1/2} \geq\frac{1}{2}C_{\psi}\|f\|^2. \end{flalign}
nodes.section: Wavelet group of the form $B\ltimes A$
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 4.1 and Cauchy-Schwarz convert the integrated inequality into a product of two $B$-integrals bounded below by $\tfrac12 C_\psi\|f\|^2$.

nodes.statement:
Since,  egin{align*} \|(\delta,\gamma)W_{\psi}f(b,.,.)\|_{	ext{HS}}^2 & = 	ext{tr}((\delta,\gamma)W_{\psi}f(b,.,.)(\delta,\gamma)W_{\psi}f(b,.,.)^*)\ &= \delta_{	au}(b)	ext{tr}((\delta,\gamma)f^*(\delta,\gamma)f(\delta,\gamma)(\psi \circ 	au_{b^{-1}})^*(\delta,\gamma)(\psi \circ 	au_{b^{-1}})), \end{align*} therefore, on using feasibility condition, we obtain  egin{align} & \int_B\int_{\widehat{L}}\int_{\mathbb{R}}|\gamma|^2\|(\delta, \gamma)W_{\psi}f(b,\cdot,\cdot)\|_{	ext{HS}}^2\ \delta_{	au}(b) d\delta\ d\gamma\ db

nodes.statement_short: Expand the Hilbert-Schmidt norm as a trace and apply the feasibility condition to pull out $C_\psi$.

nodes.name: Substitute and obtain the Heisenberg type inequality
nodes.statement: On substituting (\ref{adm}) into (\ref{cauc}), we get \begin{align*} &\left(\int_B\int_{L}\int_{\mathbb{R}}|t|^2|W_{\psi}f(b,l,t)|^2 \delta_{\tau}(b) dl\ dt\ db\right)^{1/2} \left( \int_{\widehat{L}}\int_{\mathbb{R}}|\gamma|^2\|(\delta,\gamma)f\|_{\text{HS}}^2\ d\delta\ d\gamma\right)^{1/2} &\\ & \geq\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{C_{\psi}}\ \|f\|^2. &\qedhere \end{align*}

nodes.statement_short: Substituting the simplified factor gives the lower bound $\tfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{C_\psi}\|f\|^2$.

nodes.name: Irreducibility cannot be dropped
nodes.statement: If we drop the irreducibility of $\pi$, then the conclusion of Theorem \ref{concth} may not hold. Consider a locally compact abelian topological group $G$ and the left regular representation $\pi$ of $G$. Then every non-zero function $\psi \in C_{00}(G)$ is an admissible wavelet. Fix non-zero functions $f,\psi \in C_{00}(G).$ Then, $W_{\psi}f(x)=\langle f, \pi(x)\psi \rangle = f* \psi^{\star}(x)$, where $*$ is the convolution and $\psi^{\star}(x)= \overline{\psi(-x)}$. Hence $W_{\psi}f \in C_{00}(G).$
nodes.statement_short: For the left regular representation of an abelian $G$ the transform is compactly supported, so irreducibility is essential in Theorem 2.3.

nodes.name: Support for abelian $G$ and a non-abelian compact counterexample
nodes.statement: If G is an abelian locally compact group and $\pi$ is an irreducible representation of $G$, then the support of wavelet transform is $G.$ In this case $W_{\xi}\eta(x) = \overline{ \chi(x)}\langle \eta, \xi\rangle$, where $\chi$ is the character of $G$ associated with $\pi.$ This may not be true if we consider a non-abelian compact group G. Consider $G = \mathbb{T}\times D_3, \text{ where } D_{3} = \{x,y : x^3 = e = y^2, xy = yx^{-1} \}.$ Let $\pi$ be an irreducible unitary representation of G given by: \begin{align*} \pi(t,x) = e^{int} \otimes \begin{bmatrix} \omega & 0\\ 0 & \omega^{-1} \end{bmatrix},\ \pi(t,y) = e^{int} \otimes \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1\\ 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}, \end{align*} where $\omega^{3} = 1$, $ n\in \mathbb{Z}$ is fixed and $\otimes $ being the outer tensor product. If we consider $\xi = \eta = 1\otimes e_1 \in \mathbb{C} \otimes \mathbb{C}^2$, then $W_{\xi}\eta(t,y)= 0.$ Thus, $\{ (s,u)\in \mathbb{T}\times D_{3}: W_{\xi}\eta (s,u)\neq 0\} \subseteq \mathbb{T} \times D^{3}/{\{y\}}$ which implies that \begin{align*} \mu_{G}\{ (s,u)\in \mathbb{T}\times D_{3}: W_{\xi}\eta(s,u)\neq 0\} \leq \mu_{\mathbb{T}}(\mathbb{T})\frac{\#(D^{3}/{\{y\}})}{\#(D_3)} < 1 \end{align*} where $\#(D_{3})$ is the cardinality of $D_3.$
nodes.statement_short: For abelian $G$ the support is all of $G$, but on $\mathbb{T}\times D_3$ the support can have measure less than one.

nodes.name: Groups of the type $H \ltimes \mathbb{R}^n$
nodes.statement: 1. Groups of the type $ H \ltimes \mathbb{R}^n ,$ where $H$ is a closed subgroup of $GL_n(R).$

nodes.name: $G = A \ltimes \mathbb{R}^2$ with diagonal dilations
nodes.statement: Let $G = A \ltimes \mathbb{R}^2$, where $A = \left \{ \begin{pmatrix} a_1 & 0\\ 0 & a_2 \end{pmatrix} : a_1,a_2 \in \mathbb{R}^* \right\}$.\\ A square integrable irreducible representation $\pi$ of $G$ on $L^2(R^2)$ is given by $$\pi\left[ \begin{pmatrix} a_1 & 0\\ 0 & a_2 \end{pmatrix}, \begin{pmatrix} x_1\\ x_2 \end{pmatrix}\right] g \begin{pmatrix} y_1\\ y_2 \end{pmatrix} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{|a_1a_2|}}g\begin{pmatrix} (y_1-x_1)/a_1\\ (y_2 -x_2)/a_2 \end{pmatrix}.$$ Also, $\psi \in L^2(\mathbb{R}^2)$ is admissible if and only if $ C_{\psi} = \int_{\mathbb{R}^2} \Big| \frac{\widehat{\psi}(\gamma_1,\gamma_2)}{\sqrt{|\gamma_1\gamma_2|}}\Big|^2 d\gamma_1 d\gamma_2$ $ < \infty$ \cite{Dav:96}.
nodes.statement_short: Anisotropic dilation group on $L^2(\mathbb{R}^2)$ with admissibility governed by $|\gamma_1\gamma_2|^{-1/2}$ weighting.

nodes.name: $G = A \ltimes \mathbb{R}^2$ with shearing matrices
nodes.statement: $G =A \ltimes \mathbb{R}^2 ,$ where $A = \left\{\begin{pmatrix} a & b\\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}:a\in \mathbb{R}^*,b\in \mathbb{R}\right\}$.\\ A square integrable irreducible representation $\pi$ on $L^2(\mathbb{R}^2)$ is given by $$\pi\left[ \begin{pmatrix} a & b\\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}, \begin{pmatrix} x\\ y \end{pmatrix} \right] g(u,v) = a^{-1}g\left( a^{-1}(u-x+b(v-y)), v-y\right).$$ Also, $\psi \in L^2(\mathbb{R}^2)$ is admissible if and only if $ C_{\psi}=\int_{\mathbb{R}^2}\frac{|\widehat{\psi}(\xi_1,\xi_2)|^2}{|\xi_1|^2}d\xi_1d\xi_2 < \infty.$

nodes.name: Shear group $\mathcal{S}$
nodes.statement: Shear group $\mathcal{S} = (\mathbb{R}^{*} \ltimes \mathbb{R}^{n-1})\ltimes \mathbb{R}^{n} \text{ for } n\geq 2 $ with group operation $(a,s,t).(a',s',t') = (aa',s+|a|^{1-1/n}s^{'}, t+S_s A_a t'),$ where $$ A_a = \begin{pmatrix} a & 0_{n-1}^T \\ 0_{n-1} & sgn(a)|a|^{1/n}I_{n-1} \end{pmatrix} \text{ and } S_s = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & s^{T}\\ 0_{n-1} & I_{n-1} \end{pmatrix}.$$ A square integrable irreducible representation $\pi$ on $L^2{(\mathbb{R}^n)}$ is given by $$\pi(a,s,t)f(x) = |a|^{\frac{1}{2n}-1}f(A_a^{-1}S_s^{-1}(x-t))$$ and function $\psi \in L^2(\mathbb{R}^2) $ is admissible if and only if $C_{\psi} = \int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \frac{|\widehat{\psi}(\omega)|^2}{|\omega_1|^n} d\omega < \infty$ \cite{dah;10}.
nodes.statement_short: The shearlet (shear) group in $\mathbb{R}^n$ with admissibility weight $|\omega_1|^{-n}$.

nodes.name: Reduced Weyl Heisenberg group
nodes.statement: Reduced Weyl Heisenberg group, $ \mathbb{R}^{n} \ltimes (\mathbb{R}^{n} \times \mathbb{T})\text{ for } n\in \mathbb{N}$ with the group operation $(a_1, b_1,t_1)(a_2,b_2,t_2) = (a_1+a_2, b_1+b_2, t_1 t_2e^{2\pi i a_1\cdot b_2}).$ An irreducible square integrable representation $\sigma$ on the Hilbert space $ L^2(\mathbb{R}^n)$ is given by $$\sigma(a,b,t)f(x)= te^{2\pi i b(x-a)}f(x-a).$$ Every $\psi \in L^2(R^n)$ is an admissible wavelet and $C_{\psi} = \|\psi\|_2^2$.
nodes.statement_short: On the reduced Weyl-Heisenberg group every $L^2$ function is admissible with $C_\psi=\|\psi\|_2^2$.

nodes.name: $G_{5,1}/\mathbb{Z}$
nodes.statement: $G_{5,1}/\mathbb{Z},$ an irreducible square integrable representation $ \sigma $ on the Hilbert space $ L^2(\mathbb{R}^2)$ is given by $$\sigma(t,x_2\dots , x_5)f(s_1,s_2) = te^{-2\pi i(x_2s_1+x_4s_2)}f(s_1-x_3,s_2-x_5),$$ where $t\in \mathbb{T}, x_i \in \mathbb{R}.$ Every $\psi \in L^2(R^2)$ is an admissible wavelet and $C_{\psi} = \|\psi\|_2^2$.

nodes.name: $G_{5,3}/\mathbb{Z}$
nodes.statement: $G_{5,3}/\mathbb{Z},$ a square integrable irreducible representation $ \sigma $ on the Hilbert space $ L^2(\mathbb{R}^2)$ is given by $$ \text{ } \qquad \sigma(t,x_2\dots , x_5)f(s_1,s_2) = te^{-2\pi i(x_3x_4 -x_5s_1+x_2s_2-\frac{1}{2}x_4s_2^2)}f(s_1-x_3,s_2-x_5),$$ where $t\in \mathbb{T}, x_i \in \mathbb{R}.$ Every $\psi \in L^2(R^2)$ is an admissible wavelet and $C_{\psi} = \|\psi\|_2^2$.

nodes.name: $G_{5,6}/\mathbb{Z}$
nodes.statement: $G_{5,6}/\mathbb{Z},$ an irreducible square integrable representation $ \sigma $ on the Hilbert space $ L^2(\mathbb{R}^2)$ is given by \begin{align*} \quad \sigma(t,x_2\dots , x_5)f(s_1,s_2) \\ = t\exp2\pi i&\left( -\frac{1}{2}x_4^2x_5-\frac{1}{6}x_4x_5^3\right.-x_3s_1-x_4x_5+\frac{1}{6}x_5^3s_1\\ &-\frac{1}{2}x_5s_1^2-x_2s_2+\frac{1}{2}x_4x_5^2s_2+\frac{1}{2}x_5^3s_2^2\\ & -\frac{1}{2}x_4x_5\left.-\frac{1}{2}x_5^2s_1s_2+\frac{1}{2x_5s_1s_2^2} \right)f(s_1-x_4,s_2-x_5), \end{align*} where $t\in \mathbb{T}, x_i \in \mathbb{R}.$ Every $\psi \in L^2(R^2)$ is an admissible wavelet and $C_{\psi} = \|\psi\|_2^2$.

nodes.name: Quotient $(A \times B)/(\{0\}\times K)$ of a non-compact and a compact factor
nodes.statement: 3. Let $A$ be a locally compact group with non-compact identity component having a square integrable irreducible representation $\sigma$ and $B$ be a compact group of the form $H\rtimes K$. Let $\tau$ be an irreducible representation of $B$ which is identity on $K$. Then, $ G = (A \times B)/({\{0\}\times K})$ has an irreducible square integrable representation $\pi = \sigma \otimes \tau$, where $\otimes $ being the outer tensor product \cite[Theorem 7.17]{fol}.
nodes.statement_short: Outer tensor products give square integrable irreducible representations on quotients of a non-compact by a compact factor.

nodes.name: Explicit forms of the Heisenberg type inequality
nodes.statement: Using the data given in \cite{bans;15}, one may write the explicit form of the Heisenberg type inequality when $A$ is a locally compact abelian group with non-compact identity component or $n$-dimensional nilpotent Lie group or of the form $K\ltimes \mathbb{R},$ where $K$ is compact subgroup of group of automorphism of $\mathbb{R}$.
nodes.section: Wavelet group of the form $B\ltimes A$

nodes.name: Specialization to the abstract shearlet transform
nodes.statement: As a particular case of above results, one can obtain results for abstract shearlet transform (see \cite{kam:15}) by taking $B= H\ltimes_{\lambda}K$, where $H$ and K are locally compact groups and $\lambda:H\to $ Aut$(K)$ is a homomorphism.
nodes.section: Wavelet group of the form $B\ltimes A$
